goal: Implement nextRun(expression, after) in src/cron.js to find the next matching time in a cron expression, export nextRun with CommonJS, and add tests in test/cron.test.js.

steps.title: Parse and validate cron fields
steps.detail: Parse expression in src/cron.js. expression has five space-separated fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12), day of week (0-6, where 0 is Sunday). All times are UTC. Each field is a comma-separated list of parts; a part is *, a number, a range a-b, or a step */n or a-b/n (every n-th value of the range, starting at its first value). Anything else (wrong number of fields, a value out of range, a step of 0, a range with a greater than b, day-of-week 7, an empty list item) throws an Error whose message starts with 'Invalid cron'. Invalid: '* * * *', '60 * * * *', '*/0 * * * *', '5-1 * * * *', '* * * * 7', '1,,2 * * * *' all throw 'Invalid cron'. Add or update focused tests in test/cron.test.js for field parsing and validation.

steps.title: Find matching minute and hour
steps.detail: Implement matching minute/hour fields in nextRun(expression, after). after is a Date; the result is a new Date for the first minute that matches AFTER it (strictly later than after), with seconds and milliseconds 0. Examples: nextRun('*/15 * * * *', 2026-01-01T10:07:30Z) is 2026-01-01T10:15:00Z; nextRun('*/15 * * * *', 2026-01-01T10:15:00Z) is 2026-01-01T10:30:00Z (strictly after); nextRun('10-30/10 * * * *', 2026-03-03T09:00:00Z) is 2026-03-03T09:10:00Z. Add or update focused tests in test/cron.test.js for these rules.

steps.title: Match month, date, and leap years
steps.detail: Implement month and day-of-month matching and leap-day advancement. Examples: nextRun('0 0 1 * *', 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z) is 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z; nextRun('0 0 29 2 *', 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) is 2028-02-29T00:00:00Z. Add or update focused tests in test/cron.test.js for month boundaries and leap years.

steps.title: Apply cron weekday rules
steps.detail: When both day-of-month and day-of-week are restricted (neither is *), a day matches if EITHER of them matches (the usual cron rule); when only one is restricted, that one decides. Examples: nextRun('30 9 * * 1-5', 2026-01-02T10:00:00Z) is 2026-01-05T09:30:00Z (the Friday 2026-01-02 is past 09:30, so Monday); nextRun('0 12 13 * 5', 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z) is 2026-02-06T12:00:00Z (Friday matches although it is not the 13th); nextRun('0 0 * * 0', 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) is 2026-01-04T00:00:00Z (a Sunday). Add or update focused tests in test/cron.test.js for the weekday rules.

steps.title: Search across calendar years
steps.detail: If nothing matches within 8 years after after, throw an Error starting 'No match'. Use only Date.UTC-style arithmetic (the machine's time zone must not matter). Example: nextRun('59 23 31 12 *', 2026-12-31T23:59:00Z) is 2027-12-31T23:59:00Z. Add or update focused tests in test/cron.test.js for year-boundary and no-match behavior.

steps.title: Run the whole test suite
steps.detail: Run npm test. Change nothing unless it fails; fix only failures that this plan's change caused.
